<STRUCT_0001>
An <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism of algebraic stacks should not be defined as a
smooth morphism of relative dimension <MATH_0001>. Namely, the morphism
<MATH_0002>
is smooth of relative dimension <MATH_0003> for any choice of action
of the group scheme <MATH_0004> on <MATH_0005>.
This does not correspond to our usual idea that <ACCENT_0002>tale morphisms
should identify tangent spaces. The example above isn't quasi-finite,
but the morphism
<MATH_0006>
is smooth and quasi-finite (Section <REF_0001>).
However, if the characteristic of <MATH_0007> is <MATH_0008>, then we see
that the representable morphism <MATH_0009>
isn't <ACCENT_0003>tale as the base change
<MATH_0010>
is a morphism from a nonreduced scheme to the spectrum of a field.
Thus if we define an <ACCENT_0004>tale morphism as smooth and locally quasi-finite,
then the analogue of Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0002> would fail.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Instead, our approach will be to start with the requirements that
``<ACCENT_0005>taleness'' should be a property preserved under base change and that if
<MATH_0011> is an <ACCENT_0006>tale morphism from an algebraic stack
to a scheme, then <MATH_0012> should be Deligne-Mumford.
In other words, we will require <ACCENT_0007>tale morphisms to be DM and
we will use the material in
Section <REF_0003> to define
<ACCENT_0008>tale morphisms of algebraic stacks.

<STRUCT_0004><STRUCT_0005>
In Lemma <REF_0004> we will characterize
<ACCENT_0009>tale morphisms of algebraic stacks as morphisms which are
(a) locally of finite presentation,
(b) flat, and (c) have <ACCENT_0010>tale diagonal.

<STRUCT_0006><STRUCT_0007>
The property ``<ACCENT_0011>tale'' of morphisms of algebraic spaces
is <ACCENT_0012>tale-smooth local on the source-and-target, see
Descent on Spaces, Remark
<REF_0005>.
It is also stable under base change and fpqc local on the target, see
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0006>
and
Descent on Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0007>.
Hence, by
Lemma <REF_0008>
above, we may define what it means for a morphism of algebraic spaces
to be <ACCENT_0013>tale as follows and it agrees with the already existing notion
defined in Properties of Stacks, Section
<REF_0009>
when the morphism is representable by algebraic spaces
because such a morphism is automatically DM by
Lemma <REF_0010>.
